title: Partners
section: Working with the people who decide
text:
Working with the people who decide
The hubs work directly with National Malaria Programmes — including the National Malaria Control Programme (NMCP) in Tanzania — so that models answer the questions decision-makers actually face. The network is reinforced by a regional Community of Practice in vector epidemiology and modelling, connecting modellers, researchers and decision-makers across the three countries as the project grows.

title: Evidence Synthesis
text: The unit

title: Evidence Synthesis
text:
From data to decisions
The Evidence Synthesis Unit runs a repeatable pipeline from raw data to decision-ready outputs: acquiring and reviewing existing data, re-formatting it for modelling, building shared databases and visual tools (such as MosquitoDB and interactive Shiny apps), then analysing, validating and packaging results for National Malaria Programmes and partners — and updating them as new data and feedback arrive.
The modelling framework spans species composition (single- and multi-species), spatial-temporal methods (e.g. GAMs and Bayesian hierarchical models) and explicit seasonality, driven by fine-resolution climate and environmental data and structured from national down to sub-national levels — so outputs can inform practical decisions such as timing IRS and LLIN campaigns to align with peak transmission.
Open tooling

title: Evidence Synthesis
text:
The moddafricaes package
moddafricaes — MoDD Africa Evidence Synthesis — is the unit’s R package for collating, analysing and communicating evidence. Its first end-to-end pipeline turns ERA5-Land climate reanalysis into analysis-ready data: derive a study-area bounding box from a shapefile, download hourly NetCDFs from the Copernicus Climate Data Store (CDS), and transform them into Parquet (hourly or monthly) or GeoTIFF (monthly minimum / maximum temperature).
The source lives on GitHub: github.com/modd-africa/moddafricaes.

Install
# pak (recommended — resolves system dependencies too)
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("modd-africa/moddafricaes")

# or with remotes / devtools
remotes::install_github("modd-africa/moddafricaes")
You will also need a Copernicus CDS account and an API key exported as CDS_API_KEY (see https://cds.climate.copernicus.eu/).


The pipeline

All bounding boxes use Copernicus CDS order c(N, W, S, E) — not sf::st_bbox()’s (xmin, ymin, xmax, ymax).







Function
Stage
Output




get_bounding_box()
Setup
c(N, W, S, E) numeric vector (CDS order)


extract_era5land()
Download
One NetCDF per (year, month)


transform_era5land()
Transform
One Parquet per year (hourly)


transform_era5land_monthly()
Transform
One Parquet (monthly means)


transform_era5land_minmax()
Transform
GeoTIFF stacks of monthly 2 m-temperature min / max





End to end
library(moddafricaes)

# 1. Derive a bounding box from a shapefile (zipped shapefiles work via /vsizip/)
bbox <- get_bounding_box(
  "/vsizip/utilities/province26.zip/provinces26/Province26.shp"
)

# 2. Download hourly ERA5-Land NetCDFs for the bbox (needs CDS_API_KEY)
extract_era5land(
  bbox       = bbox,
  years      = 2020:2021,
  output_dir = "data/era5land/nc"
)

# 3. Transform hourly NetCDFs into one analysis-ready Parquet per year
transform_era5land(
  input_dir  = "data/era5land/nc",
  output_dir = "data/era5land/parquet",
  dem_tif    = "RDC_Elevation_Complete.tif",
  years      = 2020:2021
)
The hourly transform de-accumulates precipitation and downward shortwave radiation per day, derives wind speed, relative humidity, vapour-pressure deficit and Celsius temperature, and joins DEM-derived elevation onto the ERA5-Land 0.1° grid. Every write step is idempotent: an existing readable output short-circuits the work, while a corrupt one is deleted and regenerated, so re-runs resume cleanly.






Known caveat. Forcing the de-accumulated daily totals to zero at hour 0 is exact only where 00 UTC falls during the night (as in central Africa). For areas where 00 UTC is daylight, real shortwave flux would be silently zeroed at the day boundary — revisit before applying the pipeline elsewhere.

title: The Project
text: Background

title: The Project
section: Climate and health in a changing Africa
text:
Climate and health in a changing Africa
Africa’s climate is changing rapidly, reshaping where disease vectors live, how abundant they are, and when they peak. That raises the stakes for vector-borne disease control and for the decisions public-health systems must make. The three hub countries alone — the DRC, Nigeria and Tanzania — account for 41.8% of global malaria cases and 46.5% of deaths (WHO World Malaria Report, 2024), which is why the network starts here. The project frames the problem around four priorities:

How is the environment changing for vectors, and how are populations affected?
How effective are health systems at controlling disease?
How adaptable are programmes and decision-makers to emerging threats?
What optimised interventions, early-warning tools and evidence are needed to respond?

Meeting those needs calls for models that are trustworthy, hold up in the real world, and keep pace with change.
Approach

title: The Project
text:
The ERA modelling architecture
MoDD Africa is built around an Effective, Robust and Adaptable (ERA) approach to modelling:

Effective — methods that produce answers decision-makers can act on.
Robust — results that hold up under real-world uncertainty and incomplete data.
Adaptable — models that evolve as conditions, questions and diseases change.

The way of working is collaborative, transparent, sustainable and adaptive: co-designing with National Malaria Programmes and partners from the start, being open about model outputs and their limitations, and strengthening the existing ecosystem rather than working around it.

title: The Project
text:
What we will deliver
Over the four years of the project, MoDD Africa aims to:

Establish modelling hubs in Tanzania, the DRC and Nigeria.
Develop relevant, model-based advisory systems for malaria control.
Share knowledge through inter-hub training, hackathons and modelling competitions, and a Community of Practice in vector epidemiology and modelling.
Form a strong Evidence Synthesis Unit.

While the initial focus is malaria, the approach is designed to extend to other mosquito-borne diseases, such as arboviruses.

title: Get Involved
text: Capacity

title: Get Involved
text:
Training and capacity building
A core aim of the project is to build a lasting network of African modellers, with capacity building embedded in how the project works day to day:

At each hub — learning by doing, on real decision problems.
Across hubs — teams working jointly and sharing methods.
Across the ecosystem — knowledge sharing and cross-learning with partners and programmes.

Hands-on training runs across the hubs in Tanzania, the DRC and Nigeria, pairing early-career researchers with experienced modellers.
Open challenges

title: Get Involved
text:
Hackathons and modelling competitions
The network runs hackathons and modelling competitions — open challenges that grow skills, surface new approaches, and connect modellers across countries and disciplines.

title: News
section: Annual meeting: taking stock, planning the year ahead
text:
Annual meeting: taking stock, planning the year ahead
A year on from launch, the network reconvened in Dar es Salaam for its annual meeting — a chance to review the first year’s progress and set priorities for the next. It drew the regional office team, country leads, postdoctoral researchers and accountants from each hub, together with the National Malaria Programme representative and the climate and environmental data representative.
Proceedings opened with a moment of silence for Dr. Prosper Chaki, Director of Resource Mobilisation at the Ifakara Health Institute, who had passed away on the 24 January 2026. In closing, Dr. Samson Kiware thanked participants for their contributions and underscored the importance of delivering the project well, for the benefit of the communities each team serves.
Read the full write-up at IHI →

28–30 November 2024 · Nairobi, Kenya

title: News
section: The network launches at its project leads kickoff
text:
The network launches at its project leads kickoff
MoDD Africa formally got under way with a three-day kickoff meeting for project leads, hosted at the International Centre of Insect Physiology and Ecology (ICIPE) in Nairobi. Technical staff, country leads and senior researchers came together to align on the project’s four-year agenda.
The first day set out the full roadmap, with the Tanzania, Nigeria and DRC teams introducing the very different ecological and health-system settings each hub will work in, and the group agreeing on first-year activities and deliverables. Day two turned to the science — malaria interventions in urban settings, early-warning systems for emerging threats, and bringing entomological and epidemiological models together — alongside a working session mapping where usable data exists and where the gaps remain. The final day focused on getting operational: recruitment, budgets, logistics, and the skills and networks needed to deliver.
The hubs left with a clear next step: convening their own national kickoffs to bring in local stakeholders, including the National Malaria Programmes.
